chapter_theme: The state of the kalas (கலை நிலை): by love turned toward Siva and by breath held steady along the kalas, the yogi can guard the inner faculties and the body, find the Lord and his Shakti dwelling within so that the body becomes Siva's temple, and by tests of the breath know when the body's end approaches and how to put it off.
structure_note: The verses are chained: each begins with a word from the end of the one before (காக்கலும் 712 to 713, நிலை 713 to 714, சாதகன் 716 to 717, கிடக்குமே 717 to 718). 721 and 723 share the refrain of the day the Lord and the Lady part (தன்னில் பிரியுநாள்), traditionally the day of death foreseen by the breath.

712.reading: If one makes love the way and looks with the eye at the forehead-eyed Lord who made love the way, by love he opens the way of the Ganga, and by love one can guard oneself.
712.nuance: காதல் வழிசெய்து is repeated in every line. கங்கை வழிதரும் is the obscure line: plainly the Lord who bears the Ganga, it is traditionally taken in yoga as a flow of nectar from the crown, or as a channel of breath. What is guarded (காக்கலும்) is not named; the next verse lists it.

713.reading: One can guard the four inner instruments, the sixteen kalas and the good breath mingled within; one can guard them all if one stands with the mind fixed.
713.nuance: கரணங்கள் நான்கு are traditionally manas, buddhi, chitta and ahankara. கலைபதி நாறையும் is read here as கலை பதினாறையும், the sixteen kalas (traditionally of the moon, matched with the breath); the printed word split hides this.

714.reading: The breath that comes evenly stands steady, still like a lamp that does not flicker; if one knows the union that stands along the path of the kalas, this is the way to be free of wavering.
714.nuance: சிலைபெற may mean 'firm as stone' or simply 'steady'. கலப்பு (union) is taken as the joining of the breaths or of breath and mind; the verse does not say which. The variant மலைவறி would give 'free of confusion' for அலைவற, a small change.

715.reading: The Lord of the elements who stays close at one's side, and the way found by holding the breath as a sluice holds water: Sankara with matted hair sits enthroned upon the bull.
715.nuance: மடையொன்றி (joined like a sluice-gate) is read as the breath held and released; the verse does not say breath. The last two lines are a plain image of Siva, and their link to the first two is left to the reader: perhaps the Lord who is reached by that way.

716.reading: People do not know how much time remains to them; one who looks to how that time can be lengthened and holds the gathered breath so that it shines stands firm, and he is the true practitioner.
716.nuance: பெருக்கின்ற காலப் பெருமை is taken as the lengthening of life by breath control, a common claim of the yogic tantra. தருக்கு usually means pride; here it seems to mean firmness or strength.

717.reading: Seeing what that practice is, one performs worship that is great austerity; if it is directed as knowledge into the place of refuge, it ripens and lies there as a transmutation.
717.nuance: வேதகம் is the alchemist's transmuting agent that turns base metal to gold; the image is traditionally of the body or soul transformed. போதகம் (instruction, knowledge) and புகலுற (into the refuge) are compressed and I can't fix what is being 'directed' (பாய்ச்சினால்), though breath is likely.

718.reading: Of itself it lies there with its three rising fruits; of itself it moves, looking into the inner nadi; of itself it spreads out as a lotus; of itself it goes on, standing within that light.
718.nuance: The subject of தானே is unnamed: it continues the 'transmutation' of 717, and may be the breath, the kundalini or the practice. The three fruits (பயன் மூன்று) are not named. The lotus (பங்கயம்) is traditionally a chakra and the light (சோதி) the vision at the crown.

719.reading: The Lady of the tattvas, who rose of herself, makes her way through the flesh and dwells within us; when the Mother who bore the world of the gods regards us, the body drinks honey and becomes Siva's temple.
719.nuance: The verse gives the body (ஊன்) a positive end: it becomes சிவாலயம் through Shakti, the claim 725 makes in the first person. தேனே பருகி (drinking honey) is traditionally the nectar of yoga; whether it is the body or the yogi that drinks is not stated.

720.reading: No one knows how the breath, which packs in so as to make one shine, is wasted away; once one knows how it is wasted, one can join with the breath in which Nandi shines.
720.nuance: அழியும் படி is 'the way it perishes', of the breath and by implication of life. நந்தி is Siva (or Tirumular's guru); the verse can be read as joining the breath to Nandi or as reaching the breath in which he shines.

721.reading: By testing you can see the flaw, the day when the Lord parts from the Lady; worship the guru, who is the means, and value him as great wealth.
721.nuance: சோதனை is traditionally the testing of the breath to foretell the day of death, and the parting of நாதன் and நாயகி is taken as death, the separation of Siva and Shakti (or of life and body) in the person. The verse does not name the breath; the reading rests on the chapter. The variant gives சாதகமாகும் குருவழி பட்டு, 'following the guru's way that makes the practice', with much the same sense.

722.reading: If you can tie fast, so that it does not escape, the horse that rose with twelve legs, and drink deeply, the body will not leave for a thousand years of water and a thousand of earth; this is the Lord Nandi's command.
722.nuance: The horse with twelve legs (ஈராறு கால்) is traditionally the breath, whose outward reach is reckoned as twelve finger-breadths; கால் means both leg and wind. நீர் ஆயிரமும் நிலம் ஆயிரத்து ஆண்டும் may be read as a huge span of years or as surviving through flood and the earth's ages; the sense is long life, the measure is unclear.

723.reading: Seven in sound, five in sight here, three in the nose and two on the tongue: on the day the shining Lady and the shining Lord part, he has set out the stainless light.
723.nuance: The numbers attached to hearing, sight, smell and taste are traditionally read as signs, counted in days, by which the failing senses foretell death; the verse names no days. தேசி and தேசன் (the radiant one, female and male) echo நாயகி and நாதன் in 721. The last line can be read as the Lord fixing the light the soul goes to, or fixing these signs.

links.note: The same charge in two parts of the yogic body: no one knows how the breath is wasted (அழியும் படியை அறிகிலர், 720), people do not know how much bindu is lost (1936). In both the knowing is the remedy: 720 says the one who learns it can join the breath to Nandi.

source_issues: 713: கலைபதி நாறையும் is a wrong word split for கலை பதினாறையும் (the sixteen kalas).
719: line 1 begins தனே, which breaks the rhyme with ஊனே, வானோர், தேனே; read தானே.
